title: Digital therapeutics and mental health apps, with Vaile Wright, PhD

sentences.en: Over the past six years, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在过去六年里，美国

sentences.en: Food and Drug Administration has approved dozens of apps designed to treat health problems, including mental health issues such as post-traumatic stress disorder, chronic insomnia,
sentences.zh: 食品药品监督管理局（FDA）已经批准了数十款旨在治疗健康问题的应用程序，其中包括创伤后应激障碍、慢性失眠等心理健康问题，

sentences.en: and substance use disorders.
sentences.zh: 以及药物滥用障碍。

sentences.en: As our nation struggles with a shortage of mental health providers, advocates say that these apps, called digital therapeutics,
sentences.zh: 由于我国正面临心理健康服务提供者短缺的困境，倡导者们表示，这些被称为“数字疗法”的应用程序，

sentences.en: could provide an important tool to get mental health treatment to people who might not otherwise be able to access it.
sentences.zh: 可以提供一种重要的工具，让那些原本可能无法获得心理健康治疗的人们能够享受到相关服务。

sentences.en: But many questions remain about how these treatments will be regulated, prescribed, paid for, and accessed.
sentences.zh: 但关于这些疗法将如何受到监管、处方、支付和获取，仍存在许多疑问。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to explore some of those questions.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将探讨其中一些问题。

sentences.en: What are digital therapeutics?
sentences.zh: 什么是数字疗法？

sentences.en: How do they work?
sentences.zh: 它们是如何运作的？

sentences.en: How do they differ from the hundreds of other unregulated mental health and wellness apps in app stores?
sentences.zh: 它们与应用商店中成百上千种不受监管的心理健康和保健应用程序有何不同？

sentences.en: What kinds of mental health conditions can they treat?
sentences.zh: 它们可以治疗哪些心理健康状况？

sentences.en: Who regulates digital therapeutics?
sentences.zh: 谁来监管数字疗法？

sentences.en: Who prescribes them and who pays for them?
sentences.zh: 谁来开具处方，谁来支付费用？

sentences.en: How strong is the evidence that they work?
sentences.zh: 证明它们有效的证据有多充分？

sentences.en: And what role might they play in expanding access to mental health care?
sentences.zh: 它们在扩大心理健康护理覆盖面方面可能发挥什么作用？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人 Kim Mills。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Vail Wright, a clinical psychologist and the senior director of health care innovation at the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 今天我的嘉宾是 Vail Wright 博士，她是一位临床心理学家，也是美国心理学会医疗创新高级总监。

sentences.en: In that role, she focuses on developing strategies to leverage technology and data to address issues within health care, including improving access to care, measuring care,
sentences.zh: 在这一职位上，她专注于制定策略，利用技术和数据来解决医疗保健领域的问题，包括改善护理获取、衡量护理质量，

sentences.en: and optimizing treatment delivery.
sentences.zh: 以及优化治疗方案的交付。

sentences.en: She's also a leading spokesperson for APA and has been interviewed by TV, radio, print, and online media, including the Washington Post, the New York Times, NPR, and many more,
sentences.zh: 她也是美国心理学会的主要发言人，曾接受过电视、广播、纸媒和网络媒体的采访，包括《华盛顿邮报》、《纽约时报》、美国国家公共电台（NPR）等等，

sentences.en: on topics including stress, trauma, telehealth, and technology.
sentences.zh: 讨论的话题涵盖压力、创伤、远程医疗和技术等。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me today, Dr. Wright.
sentences.zh: 感谢您今天参加节目，Wright 博士。

sentences.en: Thanks, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，Kim。

sentences.en: I'm excited to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: And because we've known each other for years, I'm going to call you Vail.
sentences.zh: 因为我们认识多年了，我就直接叫你 Vail 了。

sentences.en: I appreciate that.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意。

sentences.en: Let's start with an overview of what we mean when we refer to digital therapeutics.
sentences.zh: 让我们先从我们所说的“数字疗法”的概述开始。

sentences.en: What are digital therapeutics and what's the difference between them and the many other mental health and wellness apps that anyone might come across in app stores like Apple or Google Play?
sentences.zh: 什么是数字疗法？它们与任何人在苹果或谷歌应用商店中可能遇到的许多其他心理健康和保健应用程序有什么区别？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Digital therapeutics are software programs that you can access on your phone, your tablet, your computer, and they deliver evidence-based and validated psychological treatments
sentences.zh: 数字疗法是你可以通过手机、平板电脑或电脑访问的软件程序，它们提供基于证据且经过验证的心理治疗，

sentences.en: to treat things like depression or anxiety in a variety of different mental health disorders.
sentences.zh: 用于治疗抑郁症、焦虑症等多种心理健康障碍。

sentences.en: I think where it gets confusing is that these are not direct-to-consumer apps that you can download off the app store of your choice.
sentences.zh: 我认为令人困惑的地方在于，这些并不是你可以从应用商店随意下载的直接面向消费者的应用程序。

sentences.en: Those apps, like Calm or Headspace, are designed to teach coping skills such as mindfulness meditation or stress management,
sentences.zh: 像 Calm 或 Headspace 这样的应用程序，旨在教授正念冥想或压力管理等应对技巧，

sentences.en: but they don't treat disorders like depression or anxiety, and that's what digital therapeutics are really designed to do, to treat disorders.
sentences.zh: 但它们并不治疗抑郁症或焦虑症等疾病，而这正是数字疗法真正旨在做的事情：治疗疾病。

sentences.en: So how do digital therapeutics work?
sentences.zh: 那么数字疗法是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: Are they just automated versions of the type of therapies that someone might engage in with a psychologist or another mental health provider?
sentences.zh: 它们只是人们在与心理学家或其他心理健康提供者进行治疗时所采用的疗法的自动化版本吗？

sentences.en: Are they actually artificial intelligence versions of an actual psychotherapist, or do they work differently?
sentences.zh: 它们实际上是真正心理治疗师的人工智能版本，还是以不同的方式运作？

sentences.en: So digital therapeutics have taken well-established treatments, such as cognitive behavioral therapy, or CBT, and digitized them.
sentences.zh: 数字疗法采用了认知行为疗法（CBT）等成熟的治疗方法，并将它们数字化了。

sentences.en: And honestly, this constant isn't new.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这个概念并不新鲜。

sentences.en: Online versions of CBT have existed for a while.
sentences.zh: 在线版本的 CBT 已经存在一段时间了。

sentences.en: But what is new is the sophistication of the technology, like you just mentioned.
sentences.zh: 但新鲜的是技术的复杂程度，正如你刚才提到的那样。

sentences.en: So they use AI, including machine learning and natural language processing, to personalize the treatment to the patient.
sentences.zh: 它们利用人工智能，包括机器学习和自然语言处理，来为患者量身定制治疗方案。

sentences.en: So if I can give an example, let's say you are somebody who's interested in using CBT for insomnia.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，假设你是一个有兴趣使用 CBT 治疗失眠的人。

sentences.en: And your chronic insomnia issue is that you have problems falling asleep, but not necessarily staying asleep or waking up too early.
sentences.zh: 你的慢性失眠问题在于入睡困难，但不一定存在维持睡眠或过早醒来的问题。

sentences.en: And so these AI-driven devices can actually personalize the treatment and the interventions that they offer you based on what it is that you're presenting.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些人工智能驱动的设备实际上可以根据你所呈现的问题，个性化地提供治疗和干预措施。

sentences.en: So they would help you with how to fall asleep, but wouldn't necessarily give you skills on how to stay asleep because that's not what you need.
sentences.zh: 所以它们会帮助你解决如何入睡的问题，但不一定会提供如何维持睡眠的技巧，因为那不是你所需要的。

sentences.en: So that's really what makes them unique.
sentences.zh: 这正是它们独特的地方。

sentences.en: What other mental health conditions have digital therapeutics been approved to treat up until now?
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，数字疗法已被批准治疗哪些其他心理健康状况？

sentences.en: So there have been a few that have gone through the formal FDA clearance process for mental health disorders like substance use, anxiety and trauma, ADHD.
sentences.zh: 已经有一些产品通过了 FDA 的正式审批流程，用于治疗药物滥用、焦虑和创伤、多动症（ADHD）等心理健康障碍。

sentences.en: And you're also seeing them expand into more physical health conditions like irritable bowel syndrome and pain disorders.
sentences.zh: 而且你还会看到它们扩展到肠易激综合征和疼痛障碍等更多的身体健康状况。

sentences.en: So actual psychotherapy can help with irritable bowel disorders, for example?
sentences.zh: 所以，真正的心理治疗可以帮助治疗肠易激综合征，例如？

sentences.en: I mean, that strikes me as almost miraculous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这对我来说简直是奇迹。

sentences.en: Yeah, there are a lot of ways in which predominantly CBT,
sentences.zh: 是的，在很多情况下，主要是 CBT，

sentences.en: but other types of psychological interventions like biofeedback can actually address physical health conditions instead of using traditional pharmaceuticals,
sentences.zh: 但其他类型的心理干预措施，如生物反馈，实际上可以解决身体健康问题，而无需使用传统的药物，

sentences.en: which may have a lot of negative side effects.
sentences.zh: 因为药物可能会产生许多负面副作用。

sentences.en: So if we can find that, you know, psychological interventions are just as effective, if not more effective,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们能发现，你知道，心理干预措施同样有效，甚至更有效，

sentences.en: then this is another really great way to get these types of interventions into the hands of the patients that need them.
sentences.zh: 那么这又是将这些类型的干预措施送到需要它们的患者手中的一种非常好的方式。

sentences.en: How strong is the evidence that they work and how do they compare to traditional in-person therapy or even teletherapy?
sentences.zh: 证明它们有效的证据有多充分？它们与传统的面对面治疗甚至远程治疗相比如何？

sentences.en: Yeah, we've seen really robust findings from randomized controlled trials that these products, digital therapeutics,
sentences.zh: 是的，我们从随机对照试验中看到了非常强有力的结论，即这些产品——数字疗法，

sentences.en: are effective and appear to be as effective as in-person therapy.
sentences.zh: 是有效的，而且看起来与面对面治疗一样有效。

sentences.en: And we've even seen some studies that suggest that digital therapeutics can deliver a treatment intervention in fewer sessions than in traditional in-person therapy.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至看到一些研究表明，数字疗法可以在比传统面对面治疗更少的疗程内提供治疗干预。

sentences.en: So there are potential cost benefits there, as well as freeing up time for providers to be able to see more patients.
sentences.zh: 因此，这不仅有潜在的成本效益，还能腾出时间让医疗提供者能够接诊更多的患者。

sentences.en: But all that said, providers play a really important role in the use of digital therapeutics.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，医疗提供者在数字疗法的使用中仍然扮演着非常重要的角色。

sentences.en: So it's not going to replace them in any way.
sentences.zh: 所以它绝不会以任何方式取代他们。

sentences.en: But instead, providers help determine whether a digital therapeutic is appropriate for a patient.
sentences.zh: 相反，医疗提供者会帮助确定数字疗法是否适合某位患者。

sentences.en: They help them set it up and learn how to use it.
sentences.zh: 他们帮助患者进行设置并学习如何使用它。

sentences.en: And then providers need to monitor the treatment over time to make sure the outcomes are what we hope they are, that utilization is robust,
sentences.zh: 然后，医疗提供者需要随着时间的推移监测治疗过程，以确保结果如我们所愿，确保利用率保持稳健，

sentences.en: so that we can be sure that these things are working the way they're supposed to, and that a patient doesn't actually need a higher level of care because they're in crisis.
sentences.zh: 这样我们才能确保这些东西按预期发挥作用，并且患者不会因为处于危机中而需要更高级别的护理。

sentences.en: And in fact, a recent meta-analysis came out that showed that when these types of digital mental health interventions have provider involvement, they're actually more effective.
sentences.zh: 事实上，最近的一项荟萃分析显示，当这些类型的数字心理健康干预措施有医疗提供者参与时，它们实际上更有效。

sentences.en: So we think it's a pretty critical component.
sentences.zh: 所以我们认为这是一个非常关键的组成部分。

sentences.en: Now, what are they like?
sentences.zh: 那么，它们是什么样的呢？

sentences.en: I mean, if I were to access one of these digital therapeutics, what would I be hearing when I turned on my phone, put in my earbuds, and, you know, turned it on?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果我要使用其中一种数字疗法，当我打开手机、戴上耳机并启动它时，我会听到什么？

sentences.en: So the technology differs depending on the actual therapeutics.
sentences.zh: 技术会根据具体的疗法而有所不同。

sentences.en: Some are a bit more robust than others, but many have some sort of chatbot-type feature or an avatar
sentences.zh: 有些比其他的更强大，但许多都有某种聊天机器人功能或虚拟形象，

sentences.en: that would interact with you in real time and would, again, tailor the treatment based on what your responses are to various prompts.
sentences.zh: 它们会实时与你互动，并再次根据你对各种提示的反应来定制治疗方案。

sentences.en: And these treatment interventions and the scripts that the chatbot uses, they've been designed by experts in the field,
sentences.zh: 这些治疗干预措施和聊天机器人使用的脚本都是由该领域的专家设计的，

sentences.en: so we know that they're based on the best evidenced psychological treatments that exiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道它们是基于现有的、证据最充分的心理治疗方法。

sentences.en: And then you would, you know, use them on a weekly basis, maybe, you know, every five days or so as you go through the treatment protocol kind of at your own pace.
sentences.zh: 然后你会，你知道，每周使用它们，也许，你知道，每五天左右，按照你自己的节奏完成治疗方案。

sentences.en: But ideally, you know, often enough that you're seeing the real benefits, but you have that convenience of doing it from your own home
sentences.zh: 但理想情况下，你知道，频率要足够高，这样你才能看到真正的效果，而且你拥有在家中就能完成的便利性，

sentences.en: as opposed to having to go into a more traditional sort of therapy office on a weekly basis.
sentences.zh: 而不是每周都必须去传统的治疗诊所。

sentences.en: And then when the therapist you're working with is interacting with you, I assume that he or she is getting some kind of data from the app, and then what?
sentences.zh: 那么当你与之合作的治疗师与你互动时，我假设他或她会从应用程序中获得某种数据，然后呢？

sentences.en: I mean, is there some interpretation and modification as you go along?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在过程中会有某种解读和调整吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对会有。

sentences.en: Again, it might differ a bit depending on the provider, but ideally the provider is, you know, tracking the outcome data that's coming through the device.
sentences.zh: 同样，这可能会根据医疗提供者的不同而有所差异，但理想情况下，提供者会，你知道，跟踪通过设备传来的结果数据。

sentences.en: So, you know, on a weekly basis, the patient may take a brief survey, just checking to see how their symptoms are and if they're improving.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，每周患者可能会进行一次简短的调查，只是检查一下他们的症状如何，是否有所改善。

sentences.en: There are usually, you know, messaging features so the provider can provide asynchronous messages to the patient to let them know how they're doing.
sentences.zh: 通常会有，你知道，消息功能，这样提供者可以向患者发送异步消息，让他们知道自己的进展情况。

sentences.en: Or you can schedule, you know, maybe every four weeks you schedule a brief phone call
sentences.zh: 或者你可以安排，你知道，也许每四周安排一次简短的电话，

sentences.en: to just check in, see how it's going, make sure it's still working, and you still have that more kind of personal face-to-face or, you know, on-the-telephone kind of touch.
sentences.zh: 只是为了跟进，看看进展如何，确保它仍然有效，并且你仍然拥有那种更个性化的面对面，或者，你知道，电话沟通的接触。

sentences.en: So I think there's a variety of different ways that the patient still feels connected to the provider, even though they're receiving an evidence-based treatment in their own home.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，即使患者是在家中接受基于证据的治疗，他们仍然可以通过多种不同的方式感受到与医疗提供者的联系。

sentences.en: So, what's the regulatory process for approving these?
sentences.zh: 那么，批准这些疗法的监管流程是什么？

sentences.en: I mentioned earlier that some have been cleared by the FDA.
sentences.zh: 我之前提到过，有些已经通过了 FDA 的审批。

sentences.en: Does the FDA regulate them in the same way that they regulate prescription drugs or medical devices?
sentences.zh: FDA 对它们的监管方式是否与监管处方药或医疗器械的方式相同？

sentences.en: Currently, the process is very similar.
sentences.zh: 目前，流程非常相似。

sentences.en: So the FDA is tasked with regulating the space because these devices make claims that they diagnose, treat, or cure a medical disorder.
sentences.zh: 所以 FDA 的任务是监管这个领域，因为这些设备声称它们可以诊断、治疗或治愈某种医疗疾病。

sentences.en: And those words are really critical.
sentences.zh: 而这些词非常关键。

sentences.en: You know, diagnose, treat, or cure.
sentences.zh: 你知道，诊断、治疗或治愈。

sentences.en: That's the part that makes it fall under the FDA.
sentences.zh: 这就是让它归入 FDA 管辖的部分。

sentences.en: And the FDA primarily focuses on two things.
sentences.zh: FDA 主要关注两件事。

sentences.en: The first is efficacy.
sentences.zh: 第一是有效性。

sentences.en: So device makers need to demonstrate via, you know, randomized control trials and other types of research that their product actually works.
sentences.zh: 所以设备制造商需要通过，你知道，随机对照试验和其他类型的研究来证明他们的产品确实有效。

sentences.en: And secondly, they focus on safety.
sentences.zh: 其次，他们关注安全性。

sentences.en: And so that's how we get to the regulatory process in that the FDA has two pathways.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们进入监管流程的方式，FDA 有两条途径。

sentences.en: One is they can determine that a device is relatively safe, safe enough that you don't need a provider involved.
sentences.zh: 一种是他们可以确定某种设备相对安全，安全到不需要医疗提供者参与。

sentences.en: And so they distribute those over the counter.
sentences.zh: 所以他们以非处方药（OTC）的形式分发这些设备。

sentences.en: Or you can have devices that do require a level of provider involvement.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以拥有确实需要一定程度医疗提供者参与的设备。

sentences.en: And then these devices need to be prescribed or ordered by an appropriate, you know, medical provider.
sentences.zh: 那么这些设备就需要由适当的，你知道，医疗提供者开具处方或订购。

sentences.en: So in the case of mental health, digital therapeutics, that could be a psychologist, a social worker, or it could be a primary care physician or another specialty type doctor.
sentences.zh: 所以在心理健康数字疗法的情况下，那可能是心理学家、社会工作者，或者可能是初级保健医生或其他专科医生。

sentences.en: So the prescription authority sounds like it's pretty broad at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以处方权听起来在这一点上相当广泛。

sentences.en: You don't need an MD, for example, as you might with drugs.
sentences.zh: 你不需要医学博士（MD），例如，就像你处理药物时那样。

sentences.en: Or in the case of psychologists who provide, they have to go to school and get extra certification.
sentences.zh: 或者在提供服务的心理学家的情况下，他们必须去学校并获得额外的认证。

sentences.en: Doesn't sound like that's the case here.
sentences.zh: 听起来这里的情况并非如此。

sentences.en: There's a lot of confusion, I would argue, around the regulatory space.
sentences.zh: 我认为，在监管领域存在很多困惑。

sentences.en: Because the FDA only has two pathways.
sentences.zh: 因为 FDA 只有两条途径。

sentences.en: And one of those pathways is deemed, quote-unquote, prescription.
sentences.zh: 其中一条途径被认为是，所谓的，“处方”。

sentences.en: And so we all, I think, just immediately go to this idea of it's the same as prescribing pharmaceuticals.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们所有人都立刻联想到这与开具药物处方是一样的。

sentences.en: We don't think that that is the case.
sentences.zh: 我们认为事实并非如此。

sentences.en: When the FDA says prescribe or order a software, what they're really wanting is for the device maker to determine in their labeling who is appropriate to prescribe or order.
sentences.zh: 当 FDA 说开具处方或订购软件时，他们真正想要的是设备制造商在标签中确定谁适合开具处方或订购。

sentences.en: And because these types of mental health digital therapeutics use psychological treatments that
sentences.zh: 而且因为这些类型的心理健康数字疗法使用了心理治疗，

sentences.en: are within the scope of practice of a variety of different providers like psychologists, you
sentences.zh: 这些治疗在各种不同的医疗提供者（如心理学家）的执业范围内，你，

sentences.en: know, as long as the device maker includes them in the label, we believe that psychologists are able to prescribe and or order these products when appropriate with their patients.
sentences.zh: 知道，只要设备制造商将他们包括在标签中，我们相信心理学家在与患者合适的情况下，能够开具和/或订购这些产品。

sentences.en: Are digital therapeutics covered by insurance right now?
sentences.zh: 数字疗法现在有保险覆盖吗？

sentences.en: And if not, what's the outlook for that?
sentences.zh: 如果没有，前景如何？

sentences.en: Currently, there's no universal way for reimbursing digital therapeutics within our traditional health care system.
sentences.zh: 目前，在我们的传统医疗体系中，还没有一种通用的数字疗法报销方式。

sentences.en: And so, you know, you have kind of a variety of different ways that individuals might access these products.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，个人获取这些产品的方式多种多样。

sentences.en: One is you have certain systems like the VA or Kaiser Permanente who have incorporated digital mental health within their offerings to their patients within their various systeMs.
sentences.zh: 一种是你有像退伍军人事务部（VA）或凯撒医疗（Kaiser Permanente）这样的特定系统，它们已将数字心理健康纳入其为患者提供的服务中。

sentences.en: In other sorts of cases, you might have these device companies having made contracts with
sentences.zh: 在其他情况下，你可能会有这些设备公司与

sentences.en: different employers so that if you're an employee of that company, you can access the product through your benefit portal.
sentences.zh: 不同的雇主签订合同，这样如果你是该公司的员工，你就可以通过你的福利门户网站访问该产品。

sentences.en: And so I think ideally we want to get to a place where we have broader access because we have more traditional reimbursement, but we're just not quite there yet.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为理想情况下，我们希望达到一个拥有更广泛获取渠道的阶段，因为我们有更传统的报销方式，但我们还没有完全达到那个阶段。

sentences.en: In the long term, how do you think digital therapeutics will fit into the landscape of how people access mental health treatment?
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，你认为数字疗法将如何融入人们获取心理健康治疗的格局中？

sentences.en: Will they replace in-person therapy, do you think, at some point?
sentences.zh: 你认为它们在某个时候会取代面对面治疗吗？

sentences.en: I don't think that they'll replace in-person therapy.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它们会取代面对面治疗。

sentences.en: I think there's always going to be the need for high-touch levels of care from person to person on a weekly sort of 45-minute psychotherapy basis.
sentences.zh: 我认为永远需要每周 45 分钟那种人与人之间高接触水平的心理治疗。

sentences.en: But I also think that to address the mental health crisis, we need to be thinking more innovatively and we need to break away from the status quo of how we've always done things.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，为了应对心理健康危机，我们需要进行更具创新性的思考，我们需要打破我们一直以来做事方式的现状。

sentences.en: And I think digital therapeutics can be an important tool for providers to address access and efficiency in care.
sentences.zh: 我认为数字疗法可以成为医疗提供者解决护理获取和效率问题的重要工具。

sentences.en: And so I think it's going to look a few different ways.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为它会有几种不同的表现形式。

sentences.en: One example would be to address waitlists.
sentences.zh: 一个例子是解决候诊名单问题。

sentences.en: So we know that waitlists are incredibly long right now.
sentences.zh: 我们知道现在的候诊名单非常长。

sentences.en: So maybe you're a parent and your child has recently been diagnosed with ADHD.
sentences.zh: 所以也许你是一位家长，你的孩子最近被诊断出患有多动症（ADHD）。

sentences.en: You want them to have medication and psychotherapy, but the psychotherapy waitlist is six months.
sentences.zh: 你希望他们接受药物治疗和心理治疗，但心理治疗的候诊名单要排六个月。

sentences.en: Could you use a digital therapeutic designed for ADHD in that meantime while you're waiting on that waitlist?
sentences.zh: 你可以在等待候诊名单的同时使用专为多动症设计的数字疗法吗？

sentences.en: So that's one example.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个例子。

sentences.en: Another might be individuals living in rural areas that don't have a lot of access to care.
sentences.zh: 另一个例子可能是居住在农村地区、无法获得大量护理资源的人。

sentences.en: You see your primary care physician, you're reporting chronic insomnia, you don't want to take
sentences.zh: 你去看你的初级保健医生，你报告有慢性失眠，你不想因为各种原因（包括成瘾和副作用）服用

sentences.en: medications for a variety of reasons, including addiction and side effects, but there isn't any provider that does CBT for insomnia in your area.
sentences.zh: 药物，但你所在的地区没有任何提供失眠认知行为疗法（CBT）的医疗提供者。

sentences.en: So could you use a digital therapeutic designed for that to address that space?
sentences.zh: 所以你可以使用专为此设计的数字疗法来填补这个空白吗？

sentences.en: And my last example will just be, I think there's a lot of room to incorporate patient preference within our healthcare system.
sentences.zh: 我的最后一个例子是，我认为在我们的医疗体系中，将患者偏好纳入考量还有很大的空间。

sentences.en: So the example I always give is, you know, you maybe have somebody who is been diagnosed with cancer and they're receiving weekly, you know, oncology visits to treat it, but they
sentences.zh: 所以我总是举的例子是，你知道，你可能有一个人被诊断出患有癌症，他们正在接受每周一次的肿瘤科就诊来治疗它，但他们

sentences.en: have anxiety on top of it, which wouldn't be that surprising.
sentences.zh: 除此之外还有焦虑症，这并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: But let's say they don't want to come back on a weekly basis.
sentences.zh: 但假设他们不想每周都回来。

sentences.en: In addition to that cancer treatment, just to see another therapist, could you use a digital
sentences.zh: 除了癌症治疗，如果想看另一位治疗师，你能否使用一种数字

sentences.en: therapeutic that they could take home with them that a provider monitors, you know, from afar in order to really address the mental health needs and the physical health needs of
sentences.zh: 疗法，让患者带回家，并由医疗服务提供者在远处进行监测，从而真正解决

sentences.en: people in this country?
sentences.zh: 这个国家人们的心理健康和身体健康需求？

sentences.en: So I think there's a lot of really interesting opportunities as long as we can address the barriers to scalability and get these into the hands of the people that need them.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，只要我们能解决可扩展性的障碍，并把这些产品送到需要它们的人手中，就会有很多非常有趣的机遇。

sentences.en: How aware is the average provider of the existence of digital therapeutics in order to prescribe them?
sentences.zh: 普通医疗服务提供者对数字疗法的存在有多少了解，以便他们能开出处方？

sentences.en: I mean, as a consumer, I wouldn't really be able to just go someplace and find them, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，作为消费者，我真的无法随处找到它们，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, they're not in the app store.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们不在应用商店里。

sentences.en: So if my psychologist doesn't know about these digital therapeutics, how do I get that information?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我的心理学家不知道这些数字疗法，我该如何获取这些信息？

sentences.en: I think that lack of knowledge about this space is the number one barrier to getting broader access to care.
sentences.zh: 我认为对这一领域缺乏了解是获得更广泛医疗服务的首要障碍。

sentences.en: I think that, you know, psychologists as well as other providers just aren't that aware of these new products, even though we've seen a surge in them since the start of the
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，心理学家和其他医疗服务提供者只是不太了解这些新产品，尽管自

sentences.en: pandemic, I think because they haven't been incorporated into traditional healthcare, we're just not seeing as much usage as certainly we would like to see.
sentences.zh: 疫情开始以来，我们已经看到了它们的激增，我认为因为它们还没有被纳入传统医疗保健体系，我们确实没有看到我们希望看到的那么多的使用率。

sentences.en: So, you know, as part of what we're doing, including this podcast, is we're really trying
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，作为我们工作的一部分，包括这个播客，我们真的在努力

sentences.en: to get education out to both consumers, but also providers, that these are new opportunities, new tools, and to seek them out.
sentences.zh: 向消费者和医疗服务提供者普及教育，让他们知道这些是新的机遇、新的工具，并去寻找它们。

sentences.en: So, I think that, you know, APA is working really hard to address the regulatory barriers and the reimbursement barriers, and ideally, when we solve both of those, our next step is
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为，你知道，美国心理学会（APA）正在非常努力地解决监管障碍和报销障碍，理想情况下，当我们解决了这两者，我们的下一步

sentences.en: going to have to be, how do we help providers know how to use these in their practice?
sentences.zh: 将不得不考虑，我们如何帮助医疗服务提供者了解如何在他们的实践中使用这些工具？

sentences.en: How do they incorporate them into their workflow in a way that is assistive and not, you know, just another administrative burden?
sentences.zh: 他们如何将这些工具融入工作流程，使其起到辅助作用，而不是，你知道，仅仅是另一种行政负担？

sentences.en: So, I think there's a lot of work to be done, but I'm excited that APA is at the forefront of doing a lot of this work.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为还有很多工作要做，但我很高兴APA正处于这项工作的最前沿。

sentences.en: Are the companies that create these digital therapeutics, are they using the same marketing techniques that, say, the pharmaceutical industry uses, where there are actual sales
sentences.zh: 那些创造这些数字疗法的公司，是否在使用与制药行业相同的营销技巧，比如有实际的销售

sentences.en: reps who go and visit doctors?
sentences.zh: 代表去拜访医生？

sentences.en: I don't think that most of the companies are at that space yet.
sentences.zh: 我不认为大多数公司已经达到了那个阶段。

sentences.en: I think that they are still, you know, trying to determine what regulatory path they want
sentences.zh: 我认为他们仍然，你知道，在试图确定他们想要走的监管路径

sentences.en: to go down, how can they continue to get the research that they need in order to demonstrate the efficacy of their products, and how do they get them paid for?
sentences.zh: 是什么，他们如何能继续获得证明其产品有效性所需的研究，以及他们如何获得报销？

sentences.en: I do see them likely moving in that path in the future, although I would also argue that
sentences.zh: 我确实认为他们未来很可能会朝着那个方向发展，尽管我也想指出，

sentences.en: the more that we equate digital therapeutics to the pharmaceutical company, the more confusion I think we end up having.
sentences.zh: 我们越是将数字疗法等同于制药公司，我认为我们最终产生的困惑就越多。

sentences.en: So, I think it's important to really consider these as therapy tools akin to, you know, traditional psychotherapy models that we're accustomed to.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为重要的是要真正将这些视为治疗工具，类似于我们习惯的传统心理治疗模式。

sentences.en: And so, we need to pay for them similarly, and we need to just be talking about them in a very similar manner.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们需要以类似的方式为它们付费，并且我们需要以非常相似的方式来谈论它们。

sentences.en: But in the meantime, let's say that I'm interested in using one of these digital therapeutics.
sentences.zh: 但在此期间，假设我有兴趣使用其中一种数字疗法。

sentences.en: What is the average cost if I'm going to have to pay out of my pocket because my insurance doesn't cover it?
sentences.zh: 如果我的保险不覆盖，我必须自掏腰包，平均费用是多少？

sentences.en: What should I expect to pay?
sentences.zh: 我应该预期支付多少钱？

sentences.en: Yeah, the cost really varies for companies that are charging.
sentences.zh: 是的，收费公司的成本确实各不相同。

sentences.en: You know, it can be anywhere from $500 to $1,500 for the device, for the software itself.
sentences.zh: 你知道，设备和软件本身的费用可能在500美元到1500美元之间。

sentences.en: And generally, it also includes some sort of monthly kind of subscription coSt.
sentences.zh: 而且通常还包括某种形式的月度订阅费用。

sentences.en: Because a lot of these companies are just trying to get their products out to the people, some of them actually give them away from free at this point.
sentences.zh: 因为许多公司只是试图将产品推向大众，目前有些公司实际上是免费提供的。

sentences.en: So, you know, I think there's a really wide variety on the business models and the processes and the distribution model.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我认为在商业模式、流程和分销模式上存在着非常广泛的差异。

sentences.en: And again, that variety causes a lot of challenges.
sentences.zh: 而且再次强调，这种多样性导致了许多挑战。

sentences.en: If we had a bit more universality, I think we will achieve better scalability and actual access to these products.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能有更多的普遍性，我认为我们将实现更好的可扩展性和对这些产品的实际获取。

sentences.en: Let's talk a little more broadly about mental health apps, including the ones that are not digital therapeutics, are not prescribed, but anyone can access in an app store.
sentences.zh: 让我们更广泛地谈谈心理健康应用程序，包括那些不是数字疗法、不需要处方，但任何人都能在应用商店访问的应用程序。

sentences.en: How can consumers evaluate these apps?
sentences.zh: 消费者如何评估这些应用程序？

sentences.en: Honestly, it is not easy.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这并不容易。

sentences.en: You really have to do the research and you need to go to the company's website and search for published research studies that show that the products are effective.
sentences.zh: 你真的必须做研究，你需要去公司的网站，搜索已发表的研究报告，证明这些产品是有效的。

sentences.en: You need to look to see if they have mental health professionals and experts either working
sentences.zh: 你需要查看他们是否有心理健康专业人士和专家在公司工作，

sentences.en: for the company, helping to design the app, and or that serve on different advisory committees like a scientific advisory committee.
sentences.zh: 帮助设计应用程序，和/或在不同的咨询委员会（如科学咨询委员会）任职。

sentences.en: These are not often things you're going to find on the app store itself.
sentences.zh: 这些通常不是你在应用商店本身就能找到的信息。

sentences.en: So, you really do have to kind of do your own research.
sentences.zh: 所以，你确实必须自己做研究。

sentences.en: And just as importantly, you need to seek out what their privacy policy says and determine what
sentences.zh: 同样重要的是，你需要查阅他们的隐私政策，并确定

sentences.en: type of data they're collecting from you, how they're using that data, and what they're going to do with it.
sentences.zh: 他们正在从你这里收集什么类型的数据，他们如何使用这些数据，以及他们打算用这些数据做什么。

sentences.en: Because we've had some really high-profile cases lately of different online or app companies selling your personal information to advertisers.
sentences.zh: 因为我们最近遇到了一些非常引人注目的案例，不同的在线或应用程序公司将你的个人信息出售给广告商。

sentences.en: And so, obviously, that's not something you want, but it also puts you at risk for identity theft and other types of challenges.
sentences.zh: 所以，显然，这不是你想要的，但这也会让你面临身份盗窃和其他类型挑战的风险。

sentences.en: So, it's important to do your due diligence, to do your homework, to not just look at the
sentences.zh: 所以，进行尽职调查，做好功课，不仅仅是看

sentences.en: rating on the app store and use that as your way to determine whether or not this is a good tool for you.
sentences.zh: 应用商店上的评分并以此作为判断这是否是一个好工具的方法，这一点很重要。

sentences.en: So, are there different controls then around digital therapeutics that are FDA approved?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于获得FDA批准的数字疗法，是否有不同的控制措施？

sentences.en: Would they be covered by HIPAA, which makes your information confidential?
sentences.zh: 它们是否会受到HIPAA（健康保险流通与责任法案）的保护，从而使你的信息保密？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对会。

sentences.en: That's a really, really important point.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常、非常重要的点。

sentences.en: So, because digital therapeutics, again, purport to diagnose, treat, or cure a mental disorder, they are bound by certain privacy laws like HIPAA.
sentences.zh: 所以，因为数字疗法再次强调，旨在诊断、治疗或治愈精神障碍，它们受到HIPAA等特定隐私法的约束。

sentences.en: And so, they have to demonstrate to the FDA and to their consumers and providers that they are going the extra mile to protect personal health information.
sentences.zh: 因此，它们必须向FDA以及它们的消费者和医疗服务提供者证明，它们正在付出额外的努力来保护个人健康信息。

sentences.en: Apps from the app store have no obligation to do that.
sentences.zh: 来自应用商店的应用程序没有义务这样做。

sentences.en: They are not bound by HIPAA.
sentences.zh: 它们不受HIPAA约束。

sentences.en: And so, they can take your personal health information and kind of do whatever they want with it.
sentences.zh: 因此，它们可以拿走你的个人健康信息，随心所欲地处理。

sentences.en: There isn't any regulatory oversight of the direct-to-consumer, the wellness apps, the lifestyle apps.
sentences.zh: 对于直接面向消费者的健康应用程序、生活方式应用程序，没有任何监管监督。

sentences.en: And so, that's something also to keep in mind.
sentences.zh: 所以，这也是需要记住的一点。

sentences.en: So, there's nobody really making determinations whether those types of apps are effective or whether they are safe.
sentences.zh: 所以，真的没有人来确定这些类型的应用程序是否有效或是否安全。

sentences.en: So, what's APA's role in the promulgation of digital apps?
sentences.zh: 那么，APA在推广数字应用程序方面的角色是什么？

sentences.en: Is APA considering approving apps or giving a good housekeeping seal of approval for apps?
sentences.zh: APA是否正在考虑批准应用程序，或者为应用程序提供某种“良好管家”式的认证印章？

sentences.en: Is there any role that you are playing as you're reviewing some of these therapeutics right now?
sentences.zh: 在你目前审查这些疗法时，你是否扮演了任何角色？

sentences.en: So, in the wellness and lifestyle app space, our role has really been to help inform consumers on what to look for if they're looking to use one of those products.
sentences.zh: 在健康和生活方式应用程序领域，我们的角色实际上是帮助消费者了解如果他们想使用这些产品时应该寻找什么。

sentences.en: And we've also have historically had a column within our office called Let's Get Technical that's reviewed different apps in different spaces.
sentences.zh: 我们办公室历史上还有一个名为“让我们深入技术”（Let's Get Technical）的专栏，审查了不同领域的不同应用程序。

sentences.en: We also often point individuals to other groups that have engaged in sort of evaluation of these apps.
sentences.zh: 我们也经常向个人推荐其他参与了此类应用程序评估的团体。

sentences.en: But it's a really challenging, resource-intensive space to be because these apps can change all the time.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个非常具有挑战性、资源密集型的领域，因为这些应用程序随时可能发生变化。

sentences.en: And so, once you've reviewed it and maybe you've given it your seal of approval, they could turn around and change their privacy policy, and then it might not meet that seal
sentences.zh: 所以，一旦你审查了它，也许你给了它认证印章，他们可能会转过头来修改隐私政策，那么它可能就不再符合那个

sentences.en: of approval.
sentences.zh: 认证印章的要求了。

sentences.en: So, that's really challenging.
sentences.zh: 所以，这真的很有挑战性。

sentences.en: When it comes to digital therapeutics, we've really been working closely with a variety of different device companies to help them navigate this regulatory reimbursement space.
sentences.zh: 当谈到数字疗法时，我们一直在与各种不同的设备公司密切合作，帮助他们驾驭这个监管和报销领域。

sentences.en: Because I think if we can all get on the same page and work together, then we're much more likely to have a big impact on solving this mental health crisis.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为如果我们都能达成共识并共同努力，那么我们更有可能在解决这场心理健康危机方面产生重大影响。

sentences.en: Because, again, these digital therapeutics, they use what we already know works to reach more and more people to help them get the psychological treatment that they need.
sentences.zh: 因为，再次强调，这些数字疗法利用我们已知有效的方法，触及更多的人，帮助他们获得所需的心理治疗。

sentences.en: And so, I think that's really where we spent a lot of our focus is in that space because we think it can have the biggest impact.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这确实是我们投入大量精力的领域，因为我们认为它能产生最大的影响。

sentences.en: So, to wrap up, what would you say are the biggest challenges that the field of digital therapeutics faces right now?
sentences.zh: 总结一下，你认为数字疗法领域目前面临的最大挑战是什么？

sentences.en: I think the biggest challenge is lack of understanding of what these are and what they aren't.
sentences.zh: 我认为最大的挑战是缺乏对这些产品是什么以及它们不是什么的理解。

sentences.en: I think they often get conflated with wellness apps, which, again, might have a role in being helpful.
sentences.zh: 我认为它们经常与健康应用程序混淆，后者再次强调，可能在提供帮助方面有一席之地。

sentences.en: But we know that they're not used very often.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道它们的使用频率并不高。

sentences.en: They're downloaded once and then sort of abandoned.
sentences.zh: 它们被下载一次，然后就被遗弃了。

sentences.en: And so, helping people really understand how digital therapeutics are different, how they're meant to provide a different service, and how we have a higher expectation in terms of
sentences.zh: 所以，帮助人们真正理解数字疗法有何不同，它们旨在提供不同的服务，以及我们在它们能够证明有效性和安全性方面有更高的期望，

sentences.en: their being able to demonstrate effectiveness and safety.
sentences.zh: 这一点很重要。

sentences.en: I think if we can get people to really understand that, then we can make better inroads on the barriers around regulation and around reimbursement.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果我们能让人们真正理解这一点，那么我们就能在监管和报销方面的障碍上取得更好的进展。

sentences.en: People just don't understand what they are.
sentences.zh: 人们只是不明白它们是什么。

sentences.en: And when we don't understand what something is, we get hesitant.
sentences.zh: 当我们不明白某样东西是什么时，我们就会犹豫。

sentences.en: And that's what we're really seeing right now.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们目前真正看到的情况。

sentences.en: We're seeing a lack of urgency by policymakers on moving forward and really figuring out solutions to incorporate these into health care.
sentences.zh: 我们看到决策者在推动前进并真正找出将这些产品纳入医疗保健的解决方案方面缺乏紧迫感。

sentences.en: But we've got to do it.
sentences.zh: 但我们必须这样做。

sentences.en: We've got to think creatively and innovatively to address the mental health crisis.
sentences.zh: 我们必须创造性地、创新地思考，以应对心理健康危机。

sentences.en: We can't just keep doing the same old thing and expect people to get better.
sentences.zh: 我们不能只是继续做同样的老一套，并期望人们好转。

sentences.en: Well, Vail, I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 好的，Vail，我要感谢你今天加入我的节目。

sentences.en: I think the work you're doing is really inspiring and important.
sentences.zh: 我认为你所做的工作非常鼓舞人心且重要。

sentences.en: And I wish you a great deal of luck and success.
sentences.zh: 我祝你一切顺利，取得成功。

sentences.en: Thanks, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，Kim。

sentences.en: It was great talking with you.
sentences.zh: 和你交谈非常愉快。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at www.speakingofpsychology.org or on Apple, Stitcher, YouTube, or wherever you get your favorite podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 或 Apple、Stitcher、YouTube 或你获取最喜爱播客的任何地方找到《心理学谈话》（Speaking of Psychology）往期的节目。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果你有关于未来播客的评论或想法，可以发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》由 Lee Weinerman 制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Condayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的音效编辑是 Chris Condayan。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 代表美国心理学会，我是 Kim Mills。
